name: Monitor
description: Watch a background process, log file, or shell condition and get notified once when it is met.

function.name: monitor
function.description: Attach a condition watcher to a background process, a log file, or a shell check. Background processes run UNWATCHED by default — nothing tells you when they finish. Attach a monitor only when the outcome actually matters; you will be notified exactly once (when the condition is met, when the watched process ends without meeting it, or on expiry) and the monitor removes itself. Never poll in a loop for something a monitor is watching.

action.description: 'attach' a new monitor, 'list' this session's monitors, 'detach' one by id. Default 'attach'.

target.description: What to watch. Use {"job_id": "job1"} for a background process (the job_id comes back in the bash result), or {"log_file": "/tmp/x.log"} for a bare log file. Omit entirely when using a 'shell' condition.

job_id.description: Background job id returned by the bash tool.

log_file.description: Absolute path of a log file to watch.

when.description: Trigger condition(s). Multiple keys are OR'd — the monitor fires on the first one met.

on_exit.description: Fire when the watched process ends, whatever the outcome. Requires a job_id target.

on_failure.description: Fire only when the process ends with a non-zero exit code. Requires a job_id target started via the long-running guard wrapper (exit codes are not observable for plain tmux/screen/nohup spawns).

log_match.description: Extended regex (grep -E). Fires as soon as it matches anywhere in the log — including text already present when the monitor is attached.

shell.description: Shell command run in the session sandbox each tick; fires when it exits 0. E.g. 'curl -sf localhost:8080/health'.

note.description: Why you are watching. Echoed back to you when the monitor fires, so you remember the intent.

interval.description: Seconds between checks. Default 30, clamped to 10-600. Use a larger value for slow builds.

expires_in.description: Seconds before the monitor gives up. Default 21600 (6h), max 86400.
